new.title: Stroll the arcades of Max-Josefs-Platz
new.desc: Rosenheim's main square began as the market place and has been car free since 1984. Inn-Salzach style townhouses frame it, with arcades, vaulted ceilings, oriel windows and roofs with reversed slopes hidden behind tall front walls.
new.tip: Free and open all day. Walk under the arcades, then peek into the shops and cafés for the vaulted interiors.

new.title: Pass through the Mittertor and its city museum
new.desc: The Mittertor is the only one of Rosenheim's five old town gates still standing. Inside, the Städtisches Museum tells the town's story in the permanent show From Roman Grave to Kidney Table, covering crafts, trade, transport and home life.
new.tip: Ludwigsplatz 26. Plan about an hour and check opening days before you go.

new.title: Look up at St. Nikolaus, the Rosenheim cathedral
new.desc: The parish church of St. Nikolaus, first mentioned in 1315, has a 65 metre tower with a baroque onion dome that is the town's landmark. Inside you find twenty modern stained-glass windows, and organ music is played for 30 minutes every Saturday from noon.
new.tip: Free. Time your visit for the Saturday noon organ music, then walk to Ludwigsplatz next door.

new.title: Find the little Heilig-Geist-Kirche in the street front
new.desc: This small Gothic church dates from 1449 and got its baroque spire in 1684. It is built into the row of houses on Heilig-Geist-Straße, so it is easy to walk past.
new.tip: Free to look at from the pedestrian zone. Combine it with a coffee on nearby Max-Josefs-Platz.

new.title: Visit the Loreto chapel, a copy of Italy's Holy House
new.desc: Like all Loreto chapels, Rosenheim's is a copy of the Santa Casa basilica in Loreto, Italy, a major Catholic pilgrimage site. It stands on Ebersberger Straße, just north of the old town and beside the Herbstfest grounds.
new.tip: Easy stop on a loop that also takes in the Loretowiese. Peek in while the door is open.

new.title: Learn how boats shaped the Inn at the Inn-Museum
new.desc: The Inn-Museum is the water engineering and shipping collection of the local water authority. It follows the history of navigation on the Inn from Roman times to today and sits in the 17th century Bruckbaustadel.
new.tip: Small and specialist, so check opening days first. Pair it with the Schlossberg view just across the bridge.

new.title: Climb the Schlossberg for the view over Rosenheim
new.desc: Rosenheim's castle on the Schlossberg is gone, but the 460 metre spur above the Inn bridge still gives a view over the whole town. A memorial plaque and a note about the old brine pipeline mark the spot.
new.tip: Cross the Inn via Innstraße and walk up. Trees are slowly growing over the outlook, so winter and early spring give the clearest view.

new.title: See the folding boats at the Klepper museum
new.desc: The Klepper Faltbootmuseum sits in the Klepper-Park, where the folding boat yard has stood since 1919. At its peak the works employed almost 3,000 people and was the biggest employer in Rosenheim.
new.tip: Opening days are limited, so check ahead. It is a short walk from the station.

new.title: Spot the bronze Man and Horse in the Salingarten
new.desc: The Salingarten on Münchner Straße is a sculpture garden with large works, among them Heinrich Kirchner's bronze Man and Horse. Nearby, the old saline pump house at Kufsteiner and Reifenstuelstraße has boards on Rosenheim's salt works, whose first saline started in 1810.
new.tip: Free. Read the pump house boards to see why Rosenheim was once a salt town.

new.title: Cool your feet in the Riedergarten Kneipp pool
new.desc: This small city park has an apothecary garden, a Kneipp pool and veteran trees such as a Chinese sequoia and a copper beech. The Stadtbach stream runs through it.
new.tip: Free. Best on a warm day when the Kneipp pool is in use.

new.title: Hunt for the 1967 Rosenheim poltergeist
new.desc: In autumn 1967 strange events in a Rosenheim law office drew worldwide press and made it one of the best documented alleged poltergeist cases. Parapsychologists called it telekinesis, while sceptics later judged it a hoax.
new.tip: Nothing to see but the street, so treat it as a story walk from Max-Josefs-Platz. Tell the tale over coffee afterwards.

new.title: Spot the Rosenheim Cops police station
new.desc: Rosenheim is known across Germany for the Rosenheim-Cops series, produced since 2000. The town hall on Königstraße stands in for the police headquarters in the show.
new.tip: Free to look at from the outside. Fans can ask the tourist information about film locations.

new.title: Step into a blockbuster show at the Lokschuppen
new.desc: The Lokschuppen was converted in 1988 from the locomotive shed of Rosenheim's first railway depot. It now hosts large adventure exhibitions, with past themes including dinosaurs, mummies, Tibet and the Maya.
new.tip: One big show at a time, so check what is on. Allow two hours and go on a rainy afternoon.

new.title: Follow wood from forest to furniture at the Holztechnisches Museum
new.desc: This museum, founded in 1990, is in the historic Ellmaierhaus on Max-Josefs-Platz and covers wood, forestry, woodworking and wooden products. Rosenheim is a timber and furniture town, so it fits.
new.tip: Max-Josefs-Platz 4. Good for a rainy hour right in the pedestrian zone.

new.title: Raise a Mass at the Rosenheim Herbstfest
new.desc: Locals call it the Wiesn. It is the largest folk festival in south-east Upper Bavaria with more than a million visitors, opens on the last Saturday in August and runs 16 days. The Flötzinger tent holds about 8,500 and is considered the largest freestanding festival tent in Europe.
new.tip: Held on the Loretowiese. Go on a weekday afternoon for more space.

new.title: Watch the brown Mangfall meet the green Inn at the Innspitz
new.desc: At the Innspitz the brown Mangfall, the 58 km outflow of the Tegernsee, joins the green Inn. The Mangfallpark along the river has the Leuchtenwald of lamps and a viewing platform with the best look at the confluence.
new.tip: Free. Walk the riverside path in the late afternoon light.

new.title: Catch an open-air concert at the Rosenheim Sommerfestival
new.desc: This open-air festival is held in July with local, national and international acts across many genres. Tickets can be bought per day, and some days such as the family day are free.
new.tip: Check the programme and pick a single day. No camping on site.

new.title: Cheer on the Starbulls ice hockey
new.desc: Rosenheim's ice hockey club won three German championships in the 1980s. Home games are played in the SPIE Arena, which holds 4,425 spectators.
new.tip: Buy tickets for a weekend home game and arrive early for the atmosphere.

new.title: Grab coffee and a pastry at Aran on Max-Josefs-Platz
new.desc: Aran is one of the two coffee addresses Wikivoyage recommends on the main square, with a second branch at the Grüner Markt. It also trades as a bakery.
new.tip: Max-Josefs-Platz 16. Take a seat under the arcades.

new.title: Sip a coffee at Dinzler on Max-Josefs-Platz
new.desc: Dinzler is the other coffee name Wikivoyage recommends in Rosenheim, with a branch right on Max-Josefs-Platz and another by the Kunstmühle area.
new.tip: Max-Josefs-Platz 8. Order a coffee and watch the square.

new.title: Relax at Dinzler am Esbaum
new.desc: This Dinzler branch sits on Am Esbaum in the old town, a short step from the main square. It is the same coffee house name that Wikivoyage lists for Rosenheim.
new.tip: Am Esbaum 9. A calmer alternative to the arcade branch.
new.q: Dinzler am Esbaum, Am Esbaum 9, Rosenheim

new.title: Sit under the arcades at Café Bergmeister
new.desc: Café Bergmeister is named by Bavaria Tourism among the cafés on Max-Josefs-Platz. Its terrace puts you in the middle of the Inn-Salzach facades.
new.tip: Max-Josefs-Platz 15. Cake and coffee in the afternoon.

new.title: Taste Bavarian wine and plates at Weinhaus zum Santa
new.desc: The Weinhaus zum Santa is a wine house on Max-Josefs-Platz that Wikivoyage lists among the town's Bavarian places to eat. Bavaria Tourism names it as one of the old-town addresses on the square.
new.tip: Max-Josefs-Platz 20. Book ahead for evenings.

new.title: Drink a Flötzinger at the Bräustüberl
new.desc: Flötzinger is Rosenheim's last private brewery, owned by the Steegmüller family. Its Bräustüberl on Samerstraße is the brewery inn, and the brewery runs the huge Flötzinger tent at the Herbstfest.
new.tip: Samerstraße 17. Order a Helles with a Brotzeit.

new.title: Raise a glass at the Mailkeller beer garden on the Roxyberg
new.desc: The Roxyberg hill above the old town has old beer cellars, and the Mailkeller is the beer garden Wikivoyage names there. A rock chapel stands on the same hill.
new.tip: Schmettererstraße 20. Go on a warm evening; the tourist office can tell you about cellar tours.

new.title: Settle into the Happinger Hof beer garden
new.desc: The Happinger Hof is a beer garden in the south of the town, near the Happinger lakes, and is recommended by Wikivoyage.
new.tip: Happinger Straße 23. Best on a summer evening after a lake stroll.

new.title: Bar-hop down the Weinstraße
new.desc: Weinstraße is Rosenheim's small nightlife district of bars and pubs, close to Ludwigsplatz. The Ballhaus, an event venue in a former brewery, stands at Weinstraße 12.
new.tip: Evenings are the time. Start at the Ballhaus end and pick a pub.

new.title: Queue for a Saturday sausage at the Ludwigsplatz stand
new.desc: Ludwigsplatz is a favourite meeting spot, especially on Saturday mornings when locals queue at the sausage stand for Weißwurst, Wiener or Pfefferbeißer.
new.tip: Go on a Saturday morning, and finish at the St. Nikolaus church next door.

new.title: Walk the Hall of Mirrors at Herrenchiemsee New Palace
new.desc: King Ludwig II built the Neues Schloss from 1878 to 1886 on the Herreninsel, modelled on Versailles. Highlights are the grand staircase, the state bedroom and the Great Mirror Gallery, and the palace belongs to the Ludwig II palaces World Heritage listing.
new.tip: Take the boat from Prien Stock or Gstadt, then walk about 20 minutes or take the horse carriage. Photography is not allowed inside.

new.title: Explore the Old Palace and King Ludwig museum on Herreninsel
new.desc: The Old Palace is the former Herrenchiemsee abbey, and its church was the cathedral of the Chiemsee bishopric from 1216 to 1807. After secularisation it became a palace, and today it houses the King Ludwig II museum and a constitution museum.
new.tip: It is right at the boat landing, so visit before or after the long walk to the New Palace.

new.title: Wander Fraueninsel and its Benedictine abbey
new.desc: Frauenwörth abbey was founded in the 8th century and refounded after secularisation by King Ludwig I. The car-free island of 15.5 hectares has about 300 residents, an artists' colony and a free-standing bell tower with a baroque onion dome from 1626.
new.tip: The abbey itself is for seminar guests, but the island and shop can be visited. Boats run from Prien, Gstadt and Seebruck.

new.title: Find the Carolingian gate hall on Fraueninsel
new.desc: The Carolingian entrance hall of the abbey dates from the start of the monastery and counts as one of the oldest surviving buildings in Bavaria.
new.tip: Walk to it from the main landing and look at the old stones.

new.title: Circle Fraueninsel along the artists' gardens
new.desc: A path of about 1.5 km runs around the island through the artists' colony with its colourful gardens and past the abbey. Painters from Munich discovered the island in the 19th century.
new.tip: Takes about 30 minutes. Some shore sections are private, and the abbey-side beaches can be used for a swim.

new.title: Cruise the Chiemsee by boat from Prien Stock
new.desc: The Chiemsee-Schifffahrt is a private company based in Prien that runs passenger boats on the lake, and also the Chiemsee-Bahn. Boats to Fraueninsel also run from Gstadt, Seebruck, Chieming and Übersee.
new.tip: Buy a ticket for both islands. Sit on deck for the Alps view.
new.q: Chiemsee-Schifffahrt, Harrasser Straße, Prien am Chiemsee

new.title: Ride the narrow-gauge Chiemsee-Bahn to the lake
new.desc: The metre-gauge Chiemsee-Bahn has linked Prien station with the harbour at Stock since 1887 over almost 2 km. In high season a steam locomotive sometimes runs, and the harbour stop connects directly to the boats.
new.tip: Hop on at Prien station. Check the timetable for steam days.

new.title: Tour the museum of the western Chiemgau in Prien
new.desc: The Heimatmuseum Prien calls itself the museum of the western Chiemgau and shows the region's history and art history.
new.tip: A good bad-weather stop in Prien. Check opening days.

new.title: Cross the Alz where the Romans built Bedaium
new.desc: Seebruck sits where the Alz leaves the Chiemsee at the northern end. The Roman settlement Bedaium lay on the main route between Salzburg and Augsburg and had its bridge right at the outflow.
new.tip: Walk the bridge and the harbour. Free.

new.title: Discover Künstlerhaus Exter in Feldwies
new.desc: The Künstlerhaus Exter is an artists' house with a landscape garden in Feldwies, in the municipality of Übersee near the Chiemsee shore.
new.tip: Check opening dates first. Combine it with a walk in the Achen delta reserve.

new.title: Walk the Tiroler Achen delta nature reserve
new.desc: The nature reserve Mündung der Tiroler Achen covers about 1,264 hectares around Feldwies and has been protected since 1987. The river and the Sossauer Kanal cut through it.
new.tip: Bring binoculars and follow the paths along the water. Free.
new.q: Mündung der Tiroler Achen, Feldwies, Übersee

new.title: Visit Kloster Seeon north of the Chiemsee
new.desc: Benedictines founded Seeon abbey in 994. After secularisation in 1803 it became a palace, and since 1986 the buildings have been a conference hotel and cultural centre of the district of Upper Bavaria.
new.tip: Look into the church of St. Lambert and stroll the grounds.

new.title: Admire the arcaded courtyard of Schloss Amerang
new.desc: Schloss Amerang stands on a steep rock cone and grew from an 11th century castle into a Renaissance palace. Its three-storey arcaded courtyard is among the oldest early Renaissance buildings in Bavaria, and the almost circular layout has not one right angle among its 40 rooms.
new.tip: Some rooms can be seen on guided tours; the palace is also a hotel and restaurant. Check tour dates.

new.title: Visit the former Baumburg abbey
new.desc: Baumburg was an Augustinian canons' abbey until it was dissolved in 1803. Today it is the seat of a Catholic deanery for the northern Chiemgau.
new.tip: Walk up to the church and grounds. Free.
new.q: Kloster Baumburg, Altenmarkt an der Alz

new.title: Climb to Burg Marquartstein above the Tiroler Achen
new.desc: This medieval hilltop castle stands at 575 metres on a rock jutting into the Achen valley in the Chiemgau. A chapel to St. Bartholomew and Vitus belongs to it.
new.tip: Check access before you go. The valley view is the reward.

new.title: Trace the salt pipeline at Museum Salz & Moor
new.desc: The Grassau museum explains the brine pipeline from Bad Reichenhall via Traunstein to Rosenheim, considered one of the world's first pipelines. The star is the Klaushäusl pumping station, where a water-column machine by Reichenbach lifted brine, and a second part explores the Kendlmühlfilzen bog.
new.tip: Check seasonal opening. Good on a wet day.

new.title: Ride the Kampenwandbahn from Hohenaschau
new.desc: The small-cabin cable car opened in 1957 and rises from Hohenaschau to the Kampenwand's 1,461 m station. The Möslarn and Sonnenalm huts are close to the top station.
new.tip: Go on a clear morning. From the top you can hike toward the summit.
new.q: Kampenwandbahn Talstation, An der Bergbahn 8, Aschau im Chiemgau

new.title: Stand under the biggest summit cross in the Bavarian Alps
new.desc: The Kampenwand reaches 1,669 metres and carries the largest summit cross in the Bavarian Alps, a 12 metre cross on the east summit. It is also a hang-glider and paraglider spot.
new.tip: Hike from the top station on a clear day. Sturdy boots needed for the ridge.

new.title: Look up at Schloss Hohenaschau in the Prien valley
new.desc: Schloss Hohenaschau rises on a 50 metre rock ridge and dates from a late 12th century ring castle. For about seven centuries it was the seat of noble dynasties, and the industrialist Cramer-Klett later turned it into a family estate.
new.tip: Walk up from Hohenaschau village. Check guided tour times.

new.title: Ride the Hochfelln cable car to the Chiemgau viewpoint
new.desc: The Hochfelln reaches 1,674 metres and overlooks the Chiemsee. Since 1970 the Hochfellnseilbahn from Bergen has carried visitors to the summit area.
new.tip: Pick a clear day for the lake view. Check the cable car timetable.

new.title: Roam the Winklmoos-Alm above Reit im Winkl
new.desc: The Winklmoos-Alm is a broad alpine meadow area in the Chiemgau Alps in the municipality of Reit im Winkl. A gondola runs up from Seegatterl.
new.tip: Easy hikes in summer, snow fun in winter. Check the gondola schedule.

new.title: Walk the Dreiseen lakes between Reit im Winkl and Ruhpolding
new.desc: The Dreiseengebiet groups Weitsee, Mittersee and Lödensee. The Weitsee covers 63.6 hectares and reaches 9.3 metres deep, and the Lödensee is the north-eastern lake.
new.tip: Start at Seegatterl and circle the lakes on easy paths. Free.

new.title: Learn forest work at the Holzknechtmuseum Ruhpolding
new.desc: The Holzknechtmuseum, opened in 1988, shows how forest work developed from the salt-works era to today. The 30,000 square metre open-air site has moved and rebuilt woodcutters' huts from the old Traunstein saline area.
new.tip: Check seasonal opening. The grounds suit a family walk.

new.title: Watch biathletes at the Chiemgau-Arena in Ruhpolding
new.desc: Ruhpolding is known as the home of the Biathlon World Cup, and the Chiemgau-Arena is the stadium. Other sports here include ski jumping, mountain biking and fly fishing.
new.tip: Visit in winter for races or in summer to see the empty range and walk the trails.

new.title: Meet the Siegsdorf mammoth in the Mammut-Museum
new.desc: The Mammut-Museum teaches the geology, fossils and Ice Age finds of south-east Bavaria. Its star is an original mammoth skeleton found at Siegsdorf in 1975.
new.tip: A good rainy-day stop. Check opening times.

new.title: Skate or watch speed skating at Max Aicher Arena in Inzell
new.desc: The Max Aicher Arena has a 400 metre speed skating oval, and was roofed after being an open-air rink until the end of 2009. Inzell is the seat of the Bavarian state centre for speed skating.
new.tip: Check public skating times. Warm clothing helps even indoors.

new.title: Enter Wasserburg's peninsula old town through the Brucktor
new.desc: Wasserburg's historic centre sits on a peninsula formed by a loop of the Inn, and many medieval structures survive. The Brucktor is the gate on Bruckgasse at the entrance to the old town.
new.tip: Walk the old town loop and the lanes down to the river. Free.

new.title: Look over Burg Wasserburg and St. Jakob church
new.desc: Wasserburg's castle and the parish church St. Jakob stand close together at the heart of the old town. St. Jakob holds several epitaphs of local citizens.
new.tip: Combine them with the Frauenkirche and the city museum nearby.

new.title: Visit St. Oswald, Ratzinger's first Mass church in Traunstein
new.desc: The baroque parish church St. Oswald was the first-Mass church of Joseph Ratzinger, later Pope Benedict XVI, and of his brother Georg.
new.tip: Free. Combine with a stop at the Stadtplatz brewery inn.

new.title: Tour the Alte Saline in Bad Reichenhall
new.desc: The Alte Saline made Reichenhall salt from brine between 1844 and 1929. It is now a protected industrial monument, and Bad Reichenhall's alpine salt has a market share above 50 percent in Germany.
new.tip: Check opening and tour times. Pair with the old town.

new.title: Ride the oldest original large-cabin cable car up Predigtstuhl
new.desc: The Predigtstuhlbahn opened in 1928 and is the world's oldest large-cabin cable car preserved in its original state. It is a listed monument.
new.tip: Check the timetable. Views over the Reichenhall basin.

new.title: Glide across the Königssee by boat
new.desc: The Königssee, part of Berchtesgaden National Park, is a fjord-like mountain lake between the Watzmann and Hagengebirge and one of Germany's cleanest. The boat service is a main tourist attraction.
new.tip: Boats leave from the Seelände. Book ahead in summer, and bring layers.

new.title: Land at pilgrim church St. Bartholomä
new.desc: St. Bartholomä stands on the Hirschau peninsula on the Königssee's western shore, with two different onion towers and three red dome roofs over a triple-apse choir. The present church dates from the late 17th century.
new.tip: Take the boat. Walk to the lakeside and look up at the Watzmann.

new.title: Go underground in Berchtesgaden salt mine
new.desc: The Salzbergwerk is Germany's oldest active salt mine, mostly working by wet extraction, and also a show mine. It is one of the main attractions of the Berchtesgaden area.
new.tip: Dress warmly and book ahead in high season.

new.title: Learn the Obersalzberg story at the Dokumentation
new.desc: The Dokumentation Obersalzberg has existed since 1999 as a learning and remembrance site about the Nazi period at the former restricted zone. It reopened with an extension in September 2023.
new.tip: Plan about two hours. Serious content, and good on a rainy day.

new.title: Ride the Jennerbahn above the Königssee
new.desc: The Jenner rises to 1,874 metres and is one of the few mountains in the area opened by cable car for year-round visits. Alpine ski runs have ended, but visitor numbers held up thanks to other activities.
new.tip: Go early for clear views toward the Königssee.

new.title: Walk the Wimbachklamm gorge in Ramsau
new.desc: The Wimbachklamm is a walkable gorge cut by the Wimbach at the mouth of the Wimbach valley, in Berchtesgaden National Park. It is registered as a geotope.
new.tip: Check the season before you go, and wear shoes with grip.

new.title: Soak in the thermal water at Therme Bad Aibling
new.desc: Bad Aibling is Bavaria's oldest moor spa, and its thermal bath opened on 17 September 2007. The water comes from nearly 2,300 metres depth and is recognised as a healing spring.
new.tip: Bring a towel and book a slot on busy weekends.
new.q: Therme Bad Aibling, Lindenstraße 32, Bad Aibling

new.title: Ride the Wendelstein rack railway from Brannenburg
new.desc: The electric metre-gauge rack railway climbs 1,217 metres from Brannenburg in the Inn valley to the Wendelstein. It is one of only four rack railways still operating in Germany and is a listed monument.
new.tip: Check the timetable. Combine with the Wendelstein cave at the top.

new.title: Enter Germany's highest show cave at the Wendelstein
new.desc: The Wendelsteinhöhle is a natural karst cave beside the rack railway summit station, with its entrance at 1,711 metres, making it Germany's highest show cave. Of 523 metres total length, 170 metres are walked on tours.
new.tip: Wear a jacket; it is cool inside. Check tour times.

new.title: See Schloss Neubeuern's keep over the Inn valley
new.desc: Schloss Neubeuern began in the 12th century as a hilltop castle, and its keep is visible across the Inn valley from the motorways.
new.tip: Admire it from the pretty village below.

new.title: Buy Klosterlikör and Lebkuchen at the Frauenwörth shop
new.desc: The Benedictine sisters of Fraueninsel make herbal liqueurs, gingerbread and marzipan, all sold in the abbey shop. The Chiemsee Lebkuchen are available all year.
new.tip: The abbey is closed to day visitors but the shop is open. Check hours at frauenwoerth.de.

new.title: Eat smoked Chiemsee whitefish at Fischerei Lex
new.desc: The Lex family has fished the Chiemsee since 1857, now in the sixth generation. Whitefish is smoked over beech wood on the island and sold from the shop on the north shore, with a smoked fillet or a pickled fillet sandwich the favourites.
new.tip: The shop opens around noon. Eat it on the shore.

new.title: Eat at the Hochfellnhaus, the highest inn in the Chiemgau
new.desc: The Hochfellnhaus stands at 1,671 metres just below the summit cross, the highest inn in the Chiemgau. The summit chapel was built in 1890 together with the hut.
new.tip: Take the cable car, then walk up. No overnight stays, so go for lunch.

new.title: Share a giant cream puff at the Windbeutelgräfin
new.desc: The Windbeutelgräfin is a café in the protected Mühlbauernhof in Ruhpolding, first mentioned in 1553. It is famous for its huge cream puffs.
new.tip: Brander Straße 23. Share one, they are big.

new.title: Drink at the Hofbräuhaus Traunstein Bräustüberl
new.desc: The Hofbräuhaus Traunstein was founded in 1612 by Duke Maximilian I and has been owned by the Sailer brewing family since 1896. Its Bräustüberl sits on the Stadtplatz.
new.tip: Stadtplatz 20. Order the house wheat beer.

new.title: Raise a glass at Bürgerbräu Bad Reichenhall
new.desc: Bürgerbräu Bad Reichenhall is a family brewery in the spa town, run as August Röhm & Söhne.
new.tip: Try a local beer after the Alte Saline.

new.title: Taste gentian schnapps at Enzianbrennerei Grassl
new.desc: Grassl is Germany's oldest gentian distillery, in Berchtesgaden.
new.tip: Ask about distillery visits and tastings.

new.title: Sip a beer at Hofbrauhaus Berchtesgaden
new.desc: First mentioned in 1610, the brewery was the court brewery of the prince-provostry from 1645 until 1803 and has been private since 1808.
new.tip: Bräuhausstraße 15. Pair a beer with a Brotzeit.

new.title: Taste the beer of Schlossbrauerei Maxlrain
new.desc: Beer has been brewed at Maxlrain since 1636, and the brewery is a private estate brewery that has won the German federal honour prize in gold repeatedly.
new.tip: Aiblinger Straße 1, Tuntenhausen. Look for the brewery tap.

new.title: Drink at the Herzogliches Bräustüberl in Tegernsee Abbey
new.desc: The Tegernsee abbey, founded in the 8th century, now houses the well-known Bräustüberl of the Tegernsee brewery in its former monastery buildings.
new.tip: Schlossplatz 1. Sit in the beer garden if the weather allows.

new.title: Dine at the Oberwirt in Ramsau
new.desc: The Oberwirt in Ramsau's village centre was built around 1500 as a prince-provost tavern on the salt road over the Hirschbichl, next to the famous St. Sebastian church.
new.tip: Order a regional dish and walk to the church.

new.title: Eat at Gasthof Auzinger by the Hintersee
new.desc: Gasthof Auzinger is a historic inn near the Hintersee in Ramsau. In the 19th century, after several avalanches, it became the centre of a painters' colony.
new.tip: Walk the Hintersee first.
new.q: Gasthof Auzinger, Hintersee, Ramsau bei Berchtesgaden

new.title: Eat at Gasthof Zur Post in Ruhpolding
new.desc: The Gasthof Zur Post opened in 1308 as a post station and is a listed cultural monument in Ruhpolding.
new.tip: Order a regional dish; walk to the church after.

new.title: Hike to the Reichenhaller Haus below the Hochstaufen summit
new.desc: The Reichenhaller Haus sits at 1,750 metres near the 1,771 metre summit of the Hochstaufen, the highest hut in the Chiemgau Alps. It is run in summer, and you can watch the sun set behind the Chiemsee.
new.tip: Strenuous climb. Check the season.

new.title: Eat at the Seewirt on the Thumsee
new.desc: The Gasthaus Seewirt on the Thumsee is a late 19th century lakeside villa and listed monument near Bad Reichenhall.
new.tip: Combine with a swim or walk at the lake.

new.title: Swim and lunch at the Tüttensee
new.desc: The Tüttensee is a kettle lake in the Chiemgau and one of the warmest lakes in Upper Bavaria. A day-trip restaurant with a beach stands on the south shore.
new.tip: Ideal on a hot day. A swim, then lunch.
